title: Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums
title_original: 동물원 및 수족관의 관리에 관한 법률 시행규칙
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums and its Enforcement Decree and matters necessary for their implementation.

Article 2 (Methods of fact-finding surveys)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall conduct a fact-finding survey under Article 6(1) of the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") every five years (hereinafter referred to as a "fact-finding survey"). However, they may conduct fact-finding surveys at any time when necessary. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) A fact-finding survey shall be conducted by on-site survey or written survey. Where necessary for an efficient survey, electronic methods such as information and communications networks or electronic mail may be used.
(3) When intending to conduct a fact-finding survey, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify persons subject to the survey in writing in advance of a survey plan specifying the timing, methods, and contents of the survey. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(4) Where necessary, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may obtain support from zoo inspectors or aquarium inspectors commissioned under Article 12(1) of the Act, or conduct a fact-finding survey jointly with institutions or organizations possessing expertise relating to zoos and aquariums. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(5) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governors, and Special Self-Governing Province Governors (hereinafter referred to as "Mayors/Do Governors") of the results of fact-finding surveys. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 3 (Methods for evaluation of implementation of comprehensive plans)
When evaluating the implementation of a comprehensive plan for the management of zoos and aquariums (hereinafter referred to as a "comprehensive plan") and related matters under Article 6(2) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may seek advice in advance from the animal management committee of zoos and aquariums under Article 7(1) of the Act on the plan and methods for that evaluation. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 4 (Publication of survey and evaluation results)
When publishing the results of fact-finding surveys and evaluations of the implementation of comprehensive plans and related matters under Article 6(3) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall publish those results, including the following matters, on the websites of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. The operating status of exhibition facilities in zoos and aquariums.
2. The welfare conditions of resident animals, including their habitat conditions.
3. The status of safety management and disease management in zoos and aquariums.

Article 5 (Animals requiring additional specialist personnel)
"Animals prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in subparagraph 1(a)2)(a)(1) of Annex 1 to the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums (hereinafter referred to as the "Decree") means the following animals: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. All species in the elephant, rhinoceros, hippopotamus, and bear families.
2. Among the order Carnivora: lions, tigers, pumas, leopards, snow leopards, jaguars, lynxes, cheetahs, coyotes, jackals, wolves, hyenas, African wild dogs, and other comparable animals.
3. Among the order Primates: gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans, Philippine monkeys, baboons, and similar animals.
4. Among the order Artiodactyla: water buffaloes, bison, giraffes, camels, and other comparable animals.
5. Among the order Squamata: yellow anacondas, red-tailed boas, Dumeril's boas, reticulated pythons, amethystine pythons, Burmese pythons, African rock pythons, vipers, cobras, sea snakes, Gila monsters, Mexican beaded lizards, and other comparable animals.
6. All species in the order Crocodilia.
7. Among the monitor lizard family: Komodo dragons, crocodile monitors, and other comparable animals.

Article 6 (Applications for permission and permission for modification)
(1) A person intending to apply for permission for a zoo or aquarium, or for permission for modification, under Article 9(3) of the Decree shall submit the application for permission or permission for modification in attached Form 1 to the head of a river basin environmental office, regional environmental office, or regional office of oceans and fisheries, or to a Mayor/Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as the "competent permitting authority"), together with the documents specified below:
1. An application for permission for a zoo or aquarium:
  a. A statement of facility specifications, internal and external photographs, and floor plans.
  b. Documents proving the qualifications of specialist personnel.
  c. A disease management plan for resident animals.
  d. A safety management plan for the zoo or aquarium.
  e. A management plan for resident animals during temporary or permanent closure of the zoo or aquarium.
  f. A plan for education using resident animals and a plan for promoting the welfare of resident animals.
2. An application for permission for modification for a zoo or aquarium:
  a. The original zoo or aquarium permit.
  b. Documents proving the changes to the permitted matters.
(2) A permit under Article 8(3) of the Act shall be in attached Form 2.

Article 7 (Reports on the results of on-site surveys)
A report on the results of an on-site survey under Article 10(3) of the Decree shall be in attached Form 3.

Article 8 (Detailed criteria for administrative dispositions)
The detailed criteria for administrative dispositions under Article 10(3) of the Act are set out in Annex 1.

Article 9 (Mandatory days of public opening of zoos and aquariums)
(1) "Number of days prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 13(1) of the Act means 90 days per year. The opening hours on each such day shall be at least four hours. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) Days on which a zoo or aquarium is not open because of an unforeseen circumstance, such as an outbreak of a zoonotic infectious disease under Article 2(11) of the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act (hereinafter referred to as a "zoonotic infectious disease"), shall be included in the mandatory days of public opening under paragraph (1).

Article 10 (Methods and procedures for reporting temporary closure)
(1) A person operating a zoo or aquarium who intends to report its temporary closure under Article 13(2) of the Act shall submit the temporary closure report in attached Form 4 to the competent permitting authority, together with the following documents:
1. A statement of the reasons for temporary closure.
2. A management plan for resident animals during the period of temporary closure.
3. A plan for future reopening.
(2) The competent permitting authority receiving a temporary closure report under paragraph (1) shall verify and inspect whether the person who reported the temporary closure of the zoo or aquarium is appropriately implementing the management plan for resident animals during temporary closure under paragraph (1)2.

Article 11 (Measures upon permanent closure)
"Measures prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 13(3) of the Act means measures under the management plan for resident animals during temporary or permanent closure under Article 8(1)4 of the Act, including measures to transfer resident animals. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 12 (Methods and procedures for reporting permanent closure)
(1) A person operating a zoo or aquarium who intends to report its permanent closure under Article 13(3) of the Act shall, no later than 30 days before the date of permanent closure, submit the permanent closure report in attached Form 5 to the competent permitting authority, together with the following documents:
1. The original zoo or aquarium permit.
2. Documents proving that the measures under Article 11 have been appropriately implemented.
(2) The competent permitting authority receiving a permanent closure report under paragraph (1) shall verify and inspect whether the person who reported the permanent closure of the zoo or aquarium has appropriately implemented the measures under Article 11.

Article 13 (Contents and methods of animal species surveys)
(1) An animal species survey under Article 14(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "animal species survey") shall cover the following:
1. Endangered wildlife under Article 2(2) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
2. Internationally endangered species under Article 2(3) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
3. Protected marine organisms under Article 2(11) of the Conservation and Management of Marine Ecosystems Act.
(2) An animal species survey shall include the following matters: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. The status of individuals of each animal species and management for breeding.
2. The status of animal housing facilities.
3. The habitat conditions of the animal species, including temperature, humidity, natural lighting, and illuminance.
4. The status of health and nutritional management and the welfare conditions of the animal species.
5. The status of safety facilities for animal species, employees, and the public within the zoo or aquarium.
6. Prevention of zoonotic infectious diseases and the public health system.
7. Other matters that the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries considers necessary to survey for the protection and welfare of the animal species concerned.
(3) Article 2(2) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the methods of animal species surveys. In that case, "the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries" shall be read as "the heads of river basin environmental offices, regional environmental offices, and regional offices of oceans and fisheries," and "fact-finding survey" shall be read as "animal species survey." <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 14 (Exceptions to prohibited acts)
"Cases prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 15(1)3(b) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Moving resident animals for exhibition without compensation for the purpose of social contribution activities in accordance with a plan for education using resident animals under Article 9(2) of the Decree.
2. Moving resident animals for exhibition at any of the following institutions for academic research or education:
  a. A science museum under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Promotion of Science Museums.
  b. A biological resources institute under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Biological Resources Institutes.
  c. A national or public arboretum under Article 5 of the Act on the Creation and Furtherance of Arboretums and Gardens.
  d. An ex situ conservation institution designated under Article 7(1) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
  e. A facility for protecting abandoned or neglected wild animals under Article 8-4 of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
  f. A wildlife disease research and rescue and treatment facility under Article 34-4(2) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
  g. A biological resources conservation facility registered under Article 35(1) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
  h. The National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea.
  i. An ex situ conservation institution designated under Article 17(1) of the Conservation and Management of Marine Ecosystems Act.
  j. A specialized institution for marine animal rescue and treatment under Article 18 of the Conservation and Management of Marine Ecosystems Act.

Article 15 (Species whose keeping for viewing is prohibited)
"Species prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 15(2) of the Act means animals belonging to the order Cetacea. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 16 (Highly contagious wildlife diseases)
"Highly contagious diseases prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 17(2)3 of the Act means any of the following diseases: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Wildlife diseases subject to quarantine under Article 2(8-2) of the Wildlife Protection and Management Act.
2. Other diseases publicly notified by the Director General of the National Wild Animal Disease Control and Prevention Agency or the Director General of the National Fishery Products Quality Management Service.

Article 17 (Measures to prevent ecosystem disturbance)
"Measures prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 18(2) of the Act means any of the following measures: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Capturing resident animals.
2. Installing facilities to prevent escape and restrict the movement of resident animals.
3. Isolating resident animals.

Article 18 (Educational institutions)
(1) "Educational institutions prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in Article 19(1) of the Act means the institutions in the following categories (hereinafter referred to as "educational institutions"): <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Educational institutions for zoos:
  a. Zoos selected by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among zoos permitted under Article 8(1) of the Act.
  b. The National Institute of Ecology under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Institute of Ecology.
  c. Institutions selected by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among non-profit corporations established for the conservation, research, husbandry management, and welfare improvement of wild animals under the Rules on the Establishment and Supervision of Non-Profit Corporations under the Jurisdiction of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Meteorological Administration.
2. Educational institutions for aquariums:
  a. Aquariums selected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries from among aquariums permitted under Article 8(1) of the Act.
  b. The Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation under Article 96 of the Marine Environment Management Act.
  c. The National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea.
  d. Institutions selected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries from among non-profit corporations established for the conservation, research, husbandry management, and welfare improvement of marine organisms and freshwater animals under the Rules on the Establishment and Supervision of Non-Profit Corporations under the Jurisdiction of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and the Heads of Its Affiliated Agencies.
(2) The head of an educational institution shall issue a certificate of completion in attached Form 6 to a person who completes education and shall report the education provided for each zoo and aquarium during the year to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries by the end of February of the following year. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the competent permitting authority of the education provided for each zoo or aquarium as reported under paragraph (2). <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(4) The head of an educational institution shall formulate an education plan for the following year and submit it to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries by December 31 each year. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(5) Matters necessary for conducting education other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4) shall be determined by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 19 (Contents and duration of education)
A person subject to education under Article 19(1) of the Act shall receive education conducted by an educational institution at least once each year. The contents and duration of education for each category of persons subject to education are set out in Annex 2.

Article 20 (Keeping and preservation of operation and management records)
"Matters prescribed by Joint Decree of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries" in subparagraph 4 of Article 20 of the Act means the following matters: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Records concerning management of and changes to animal housing facilities.
2. Records of the status of veterinarians, aquatic organism disease inspectors, and animal keepers employed.
3. Records concerning treatment of diseases of resident animals.
4. Records concerning safety accidents at the zoo or aquarium.

Article 21 (Timing and methods of inspections of zoos and aquariums)
(1) The competent permitting authority shall conduct inspections under Article 22(1) of the Act in the following categories:
1. Periodic inspection: once every five years after permission is granted.
2. Ad hoc inspection: where the competent permitting authority considers it necessary to verify the actual conditions of the zoo's or aquarium's facilities and equipment, the management of resident animals, or the working status of employees.
(2) When conducting a periodic inspection under paragraph (1)1, the competent permitting authority shall verify:
1. Compliance with the requirements for permission under Article 8(1) of the Act.
2. Compliance with the management plan during temporary closure under Article 13(2) of the Act.
3. Whether the prohibitions under Article 15 of the Act have been violated.
4. Compliance with Articles 16 through 18 of the Act.
5. Whether persons subject to education have completed education under Article 19 of the Act.
(3) When intending to conduct an inspection under paragraph (1), the competent permitting authority shall notify the person operating the zoo or aquarium in writing in advance of an inspection plan specifying the date and time, subject, and contents of the inspection.
(4) Upon completion of an inspection under paragraph (1), the competent permitting authority shall submit the results to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within 30 days from the date of completion. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 22 (Designation and operation of hub zoos and hub aquariums)
(1) A person intending to be designated as a hub zoo or hub aquarium under Article 24(2) of the Act shall submit the application for designation as a hub zoo or hub aquarium in attached Form 7 to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, together with the following materials: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. A statement of facility specifications, internal and external photographs, and floor plans.
2. The status of personnel and equipment.
3. A detailed statement of resident animals.
4. Materials proving satisfaction of the requirements for designation as a hub zoo or hub aquarium.
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries receiving an application under paragraph (1) shall determine whether to designate the applicant as a hub zoo or hub aquarium and shall issue a designation certificate in attached Form 8. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) The designation period for a hub zoo or hub aquarium shall not exceed five years.
(4) A person designated as a hub zoo or hub aquarium shall establish operating guidelines for the hub zoo or hub aquarium and obtain approval from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(5) A person designated as a hub zoo or hub aquarium shall submit the operating plan for the current year and the operating results for the preceding year to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries by January 31 each year. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 23 (Procedures for accepting donations)
(1) A zoo or aquarium established by the State, a local government, or an affiliated agency thereof, or established with investment or contributions from the State or a local government (hereinafter in this Article referred to as a "public zoo or aquarium"), shall issue a receipt to the donor when accepting money or goods voluntarily donated under Article 26(1) of the Act (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "donations"). However, a receipt need not be issued where the donation is anonymous or the donor is unknown.
(2) Where a donor under paragraph (1) specifies the purpose for which a donation is to be used, a public zoo or aquarium shall use it only for that purpose. However, where a special reason makes it difficult to use the donation for the purpose specified by the donor, it may be used for another purpose with the donor's consent after consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) A public zoo or aquarium shall maintain books recording the status of acceptance and use of donations and other relevant matters and make them available for inspection by donors.

Article 24 (Review of regulations)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall review the appropriateness of the contents and duration of education for each category of persons subject to education under Article 19 and Annex 2 every three years from January 1, 2024 (meaning before January 1 of each third year), and shall take measures such as making improvements. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

ADDENDA <No. 640, December 14, 2023>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Rule shall enter into force on December 14, 2023. However, the amended Article 19 shall enter into force on January 1, 2024, and the amended subparagraph 1 of Article 16 shall enter into force on May 19, 2024.

Article 2 (Special provisions concerning mandatory days of public opening of zoos and aquariums)
When applying the mandatory days of public opening to a zoo or aquarium operating at the time this Rule enters into force, the mandatory number of days shall be 30 through December 31, 2023, notwithstanding the amended Article 9(1).

ADDENDA (Enforcement Rule on the Organization of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and Its Affiliated Agencies) <No. 1, October 1, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Rule shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. However, amendments under Article 6 of these Addenda to ministerial ordinances promulgated before this Rule enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall each enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant ministerial ordinance.

Articles 2 through 5 Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendments to other statutes or regulations)
(1) through (17) Omitted.

(18) The Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums is partially amended as follows:

In the main clause of Article 2(1), Article 2(3) through (5), Article 3, the portion of Article 4 preceding its subparagraphs, Article 13(2)7, the latter sentence of Article 13(3), Article 18(1)1(a) and (c), Article 18(2) through (5), Article 21(4), the portion of Article 22(1) preceding its subparagraphs, Article 22(2), (4), and (5), the proviso to Article 23(2), and Article 24, "Minister of Environment" is each replaced by "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment."

In the portion of Article 4 preceding its subparagraphs, "Ministry of Environment and" is replaced by "Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and"; and in the portion of Article 5 preceding its subparagraphs, the first sentence of Article 9(1), Article 11, the portion of Article 14 preceding its subparagraphs, Article 15, the portions of Articles 16 and 17 preceding their respective subparagraphs, the portion of Article 18(1) preceding its subparagraphs, and the portion of Article 20 preceding its subparagraphs, "Ministry of Environment" is replaced by "Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment."

In Article 18(1)1(c), "Rules on the Establishment and Supervision of Non-Profit Corporations under the Jurisdiction of the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Meteorological Administration" is replaced by "Rules on the Establishment and Supervision of Non-Profit Corporations under the Jurisdiction of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Meteorological Administration."

In attached Forms 7 and 8, "Minister of Environment" is each replaced by "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment."

(19) through (98) Omitted.

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE MANAGEMENT OF ZOOS AND AQUARIUMS
[Annex 1]

Detailed criteria for administrative dispositions (related to Article 8)

1. General criteria

  a. Where two or more violations have occurred and different disposition criteria apply to them, the more severe criteria shall apply. Where the criteria for two or more violations are all suspension of business, the more severe suspension period may be increased by up to one half of that period, provided that the resulting period does not exceed the sum of the periods under the respective disposition criteria.
  b. Criteria based on the number of violations apply where an administrative disposition has been imposed for the same violation within the preceding year. The period shall be calculated by reference to the date on which the administrative disposition for the violation was imposed (where a penalty surcharge was imposed in place of suspension of business, the date of imposition of that surcharge) and the date on which the same violation committed again after that disposition was detected.
  c. When imposing an aggravated disposition under item b, the applicable level shall be the level following that of the disposition before the violation. Where two or more dispositions were imposed within the period under item b, the higher level shall be used.
  d. The authority making the disposition may increase or reduce the applicable disposition by up to one half of the prescribed level, taking account of the motive, nature, and number of violations, the severity of the violation, the harm to the public interest, and other relevant circumstances.

2. Individual criteria

| Violation | Statutory basis | First violation | Second violation | Third violation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Obtaining permission by fraud or other improper means | Article 10(1)1 of the Act | Revocation of permission | | |
| 2. Ceasing to satisfy the requirements for permission under Article 8(1) or (2) of the Act | Article 10(1)2 of the Act | Suspension of business for one month | Suspension of business for three months | Revocation of permission |
| 3. Falling under a ground for disqualification in subparagraphs 1 through 6 or 8 of Article 9 of the Act; however, excluding a corporation with an executive officer falling under subparagraph 8 of that Article that replaces the executive officer within six months | Article 10(1)3 of the Act | Warning | Suspension of business for one month | Suspension of business for three months |
| 4. Failing to comply with an order to take measures under Article 23 of the Act | Article 10(1)4 of the Act | Suspension of business for one month | Suspension of business for three months | Revocation of permission |

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE MANAGEMENT OF ZOOS AND AQUARIUMS
[Annex 2]

Contents and duration of education by category of persons subject to education (related to Article 19)

| Persons subject to education | Contents of education | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Veterinarians and aquatic organism disease inspectors under Article 19(1)1 of the Act; 2. Persons assisting with veterinary work or aquatic organism disease management under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Decree | Common education | Four hours |
| Categories 1 and 2 above | Specialized education: veterinary and aquatic organism disease management clinical practice, disease prevention and control, quarantine, health management of resident animals, and related subjects | Four hours |
| 3. Animal keepers under Article 19(1)2 of the Act; 4. Persons assisting with animal husbandry under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Decree | Common education | Four hours |
| Categories 3 and 4 above | Specialized education: behavioral enrichment, positive reinforcement, safety management, habitat and nutritional management, animal welfare, and related subjects | Four hours |
| 5. Persons other than those in categories 1 through 4 who have worked continuously at a zoo or aquarium for at least one year under subparagraph 2 of Article 19 of the Decree | Common education | Four hours |

Notes:
1. Common education shall include basic knowledge that executives and employees of zoos or aquariums should share, including disease prevention and control and public hygiene, disaster and safety management, accident prevention, animal welfare, ecological characteristics and habits of each animal species, and operation of water quality management and life support systems (LSS).
2. Persons subject to education may complete common education at either an educational institution for zoos or an educational institution for aquariums, regardless of that distinction. For specialized education, persons working at zoos shall complete it at educational institutions for zoos, and persons working at aquariums shall complete it at educational institutions for aquariums.
3. Common education and specialized education may be conducted as group education or online education.
